changelog: Initial version: the desk's revenue-reconciliation method, written for the skills library.
description: Reconcile a headline revenue figure across every document that states it, naming each bridge item instead of blending figures.
method:
METHOD: REVENUE BRIDGE — run this before recording any revenue finding.

1. Start from the primary source. Find the filing or annual report that states revenue for the period and read it in full. Its figure is the anchor: record it first, in the ledger's own words, with its fact reference.
2. Walk every other document that states a revenue figure for the same period — preliminary releases, investor updates, trade coverage. Read each one; do not rely on search excerpts for a number you will record.
3. For each figure that differs from the anchor, name the bridge item before you record it: preliminary versus final, restated versus as-first-reported, segment versus group total, a different period wearing the same label, or a plain disagreement. The bridge item goes in your summary line, never in the claim — claims stay in the ledger's words.
4. Record every figure as its own finding, each citing the document that states it. Two documents stating two figures for one period is a conflict for the desk's machinery to surface, not a discrepancy for you to settle: never average two figures, never silently prefer the newer one, and never state a reconciled total that no single document states.
5. If a document states a figure its own Key facts ledger does not carry, record the claim without a fact reference and say so in your summary — prose is not a ledger.

The bridge is the deliverable: an analyst reading your findings should be able to walk from the anchor figure to every other figure in the case, one named item at a time.
name: revenue-bridge
